# System

Requirements extracted from [`SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md). This view is for focused reading and review; the spec text is normative.

## SR

- **SR-1** — Every run MUST be fully determined by a configuration file derived from `params.generated.yaml`; no experiment-affecting constant may be hard-coded in source. *(verify: unit test asserting config round-trip, plus a lint rule flagging numeric SNR/k literals outside `src/config/` and tests)*
- **SR-2** — All datasets in `params.datasets` MUST be selectable by name through one code path, with no dataset-specific branching in the encoder, decoder or training loop (DEC-1). *(verify: unit test instantiating each dataset)*
- **SR-3** — For a configured dataset and ratio, the encoder MUST emit exactly the number of complex symbols given by `params.bandwidth.k_symbols`. *(verify: unit test on output shape for every dataset × ratio pair)*
- **SR-4** — Transmitted symbols MUST satisfy `params.bandwidth.power_constraint` per image via an explicit normalisation layer, so SNR is unambiguous. *(verify: unit test that empirical mean power is 1.0 ± 1e-3)*
- **SR-5** — Channel models MUST live behind a registry exposing `forward(x, snr_db)` and be selectable by name. `params.channel.models_supported` is required now; `params.channel.models_planned` MUST be addable without modifying encoder, decoder or training code (FW-1). *(verify: unit test registering a stub channel and training one step through it)*
- **SR-6** — The channel MUST be differentiable end-to-end; gradients from the loss MUST reach encoder parameters. *(verify: unit test asserting non-zero encoder gradients after one backward pass)*
- **SR-7** — Noise power MUST be derived from `params.channel.snr_definition` alone, and the same definition MUST be used by the learned system, the baseline and the hardware tiers. *(verify: unit test measuring empirical SNR against the requested value)*
- **SR-8** — The decoder MUST carry both heads in `params.learned_system.decoder_heads`, trained as `params.learned_system.loss` with λ read from config (DEC-2). Setting λ = 0 MUST yield a pure-task model without code changes (FW-2). *(verify: unit test on both head outputs and on λ=0 disabling the MSE term)*
- **SR-9** — λ MUST be calibrated at G-4, **on the validation split** (DEC-12), to the smallest value in `params.learned_system.lambda_grid` whose top-1 accuracy at `params.learned_system.lambda_calibration_snr_db` is within `params.learned_system.lambda_acc_tolerance_pp` of the λ=0 model while reconstruction PSNR at `params.learned_system.lambda_psnr_eval_snr_db` is at least `params.learned_system.lambda_psnr_floor_db`, falling back to `params.learned_system.lambda_psnr_floor_relaxed_db` before any DEC-2 model split. Calibration happens at `params.learned_system.lambda_calibration_ratio` and the chosen λ transfers to the other ratios DEC-11 trains. Those three parameters replace the phrases "the core SNR" and "15 dB SNR", which named no parameter at all and were bare numeric literals of exactly the kind SR-1's own lint rule exists to flag — the requirement and its linter disagreed (AM-35). DEC-2's relaxed PSNR floor exists partly to absorb λ's transfer to smaller ratios, where the floor is harder to clear. The chosen value MUST replace `params.learned_system.lambda_core` in this file and clear `lambda_status`. The search is one pilot training run per grid entry at a single seed, so G-4's cost is bounded in advance rather than open-ended; and because λ sits in the training objective, the final multi-seed training of §13 MUST happen **after** this gate, never before it (AM-7). *(verify: calibration run archived under `params.artifacts.results_dir`, one row per `params.learned_system.lambda_grid` entry)*
- **SR-10** — Training MUST checkpoint every `params.compute.checkpoint_every_epochs` epochs and resume from checkpoint with no metric discontinuity, so runs survive Colab/Kaggle session limits (DEC-4). *(verify: kill-and-resume test comparing loss curves across the seam)*
- **SR-11** — A profiling run at `params.compute.profiling_gate` MUST establish the achievable batch size, epoch time and peak memory on `params.compute.primary_device`; thereafter no scheduled run may exceed `params.compute.max_wall_clock_hours_per_run` or `params.compute.vram_budget_gb`, and sweeps MUST be decomposable into independent runs each meeting those bounds. `params.learned_system.batch_size` is a target, not a constraint: gradient accumulation per `params.learned_system.grad_accumulation_allowed` MAY be used to hold the effective batch size. *(verify: profiling report archived, and measured wall clock and peak VRAM logged per run)*
- **SR-12** — Runs MUST be deterministic given a seed: on the same pinned software environment and hardware class, the same seed and config reproduce reported metrics within 0.5 percentage points; across environments, reproduction is required only within the reported interval. The lockfile, CUDA and driver versions MUST be recorded with the results. *(verify: repeat-run test on the pinned environment plus an archived environment manifest)*
- **SR-13** — Every result row MUST record its `run_id`, `git_commit`, `git_dirty` and `config_hash`, and artifacts MUST be written under the directories in `params.artifacts`. *(verify: schema test on emitted CSV)*
- **SR-14** — The learned model MUST NOT exceed `params.learned_system.max_params_millions` million parameters. The binding justification is `params.learned_system.max_params_policy`: encoder, decoder and head together MUST NOT exceed the parameter count of `params.reference_classifier`, so the learned arm is never larger than the network scoring the classical arm. This replaces the original rationale — "keeping the RPi tier plausible" — which rested a Tier 1 constraint on a stretch tier that DEC-14 makes explicit upside and HR-5 forbids any Tier 1 requirement from depending on. The numbers happen to coincide: a ResNet-18 at ten classes is about 11.2M parameters, so the 10M cap is already below its own comparator and the re-justification costs nothing (AM-36). *(verify: unit test on parameter count, asserting both the absolute cap and that it does not exceed the measured reference-classifier count)*
- **SR-15** — The downstream task head MUST sit behind a registry so a different task can be added without touching the encoder, channel or training loop (FW-4). *(verify: unit test registering a stub task head)*
- **SR-16** — Peak-to-average power ratio MUST be measured and reported per `params.learned_system.papr_report_required` for **all three systems**, not the learned one alone — adaptive 16-QAM is not constant modulus either, so reporting the learned arm's PAPR in isolation invites the reader to assume the digital arms are at 0 dB. A peak-power/clipping constraint MUST be available per `params.learned_system.peak_power_constraint_available`, and per `params.learned_system.papr_constrained_variant_required` a PAPR-constrained learned variant MUST be trained and reported as a secondary curve at `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` over `params.learned_system.papr_constrained_variant_seeds` seed. Rationale: an average-power constraint lets a learned encoder buy SNR with peaky symbols that a constant-modulus scheme cannot use and a real amplifier cannot deliver; unreported, this is an unearned advantage in simulation and a Tier 2 discrepancy on hardware. Disclosure alone answers "did you know?" but not "is the comparison fair?", and this is the first objection a reader with a communications background reaches for — one extra training run converts it into a figure this project produced itself (AM-44). Reported PAPR is the **symbol-domain** peak-to-average ratio; oversampled waveform PAPR after pulse shaping is a different and larger quantity, and the two MUST NOT be conflated in the report. *(verify: PAPR logged in every result row for every system, a unit test that the clipping constraint bounds measured PAPR, and the constrained variant present as a distinct `system` value)*
- **SR-17** — A validation split MUST be carved per `params.evaluation.split_rule` from each dataset's `val_images` count and used for **every** selection decision — baseline configuration, λ, training checkpoint, operating ratio, architecture (DEC-12). The test split MUST NOT be read by any selection code path. **A seed is not a portable split specification (AM-58).** Loader ordering and library behaviour can change between versions, so the split MUST be materialised as a committed manifest under `params.datasets.manifest_dir` in `params.datasets.manifest_format`, listing every `params.datasets.stable_sample_id_rule` identifier with its label and split assignment, and hashed into the run metadata. The carve MUST be stratified per `params.datasets.split_carve_stratified`, ordered per `params.datasets.split_pre_shuffle_order` before shuffling, and drawn with `params.datasets.split_rng` — an unordered starting point makes `params.evaluation.split_seed` reproduce nothing. Class indices come from `params.datasets.class_index_source`, so a relabelled directory listing cannot silently permute the label space. *(verify: unit test asserting split disjointness and exact counts against `params.datasets`; a test that the committed manifest hash reproduces from a clean checkout; a test that class-to-index mapping matches the manifest; and an audit that no selection routine can reach the test loader)*
- **SR-18** — Every evaluation run MUST emit a per-image outcome file matching `params.artifacts.per_image_schema` under `params.artifacts.per_image_dir`. **Identity and pairing are separate keys and MUST NOT be conflated (AM-58).** `run_id` identifies *one system's run* and MUST be unique per `params.artifacts.run_id_key`, formed per `params.artifacts.run_id_form`; `params.artifacts.pair_id_key` builds a **system-independent** `pair_id` that both arms of a comparison share, excluding everything in `params.artifacts.pair_id_excludes`; `params.artifacts.noise_id_key` identifies the channel realisation a row was drawn under; and `params.artifacts.analysis_cell_id_key` names the compound replicate. ER-10 joins on `pair_id`, so one learned per-image row participates in both the learned-versus-classical and the learned-versus-ER-9 comparisons without being duplicated. This replaces "ER-10 pairs per-image outcomes across systems at matched (image, SNR, seed) *entirely through `run_id`*" (AM-37), which was unsound in both directions: `run_id_key` contains `system`, so the two arms never shared an ID, while it omitted `split`, the config and checkpoint hashes, the classifier variant and every system-specific setting — so a validation run and a test run, or the two BR-12 classifier variants, or two cells of ER-9's width search, **collided on the same ID**. `params.artifacts.rng_stream` requires counter-based keyed streams over `params.artifacts.rng_purposes`: a shared integer seed with conditionally consumed draws does not guarantee common noise across systems whose control flow differs, which is exactly what happens when one system outages on an image and another does not. *(verify: schema test; a test that recomputing `top1_acc` from the per-image file matches the aggregate row; a test that no two result rows share a `run_id` with differing `params.artifacts.run_id_key` values; a test that row reordering and batching change no `noise_id` and no draw; a test that two systems in one comparison cell share `pair_id` and `noise_id` while holding distinct `run_id`s; a test that changing split, checkpoint or config always changes `run_id`; a test that changing system never changes `pair_id`; and a test that the ER-10 join is one-to-one and rejects missing or duplicated trajectories)*
- **SR-19** — One canonical image MUST be defined per `params.preprocessing` and produced **before** either pipeline sees the data: `canonical_image`, `resize_interpolation`, `antialias`, `train_crop`, `eval_crop`, `colour_space`, `bit_depth` and `tensor_range`, with `eval_augmentation_permitted` false and `channel_normalisation` applied inside the model rather than in the pipeline. **Every free parameter of that pipeline is now fixed rather than left to a library default (AM-58),** because each one changes a reported number and none of them were specified: `params.preprocessing.train_crop_scale` and `train_crop_ratio` for the random resized crop, `train_hflip_p` for the flip, `channel_mean` and `channel_std` for the in-model normalisation, and `params.preprocessing.canonical_and_augmentation_are_separate_stages` settling that canonicalisation and training augmentation are two stages rather than one fused transform — which is what makes "the codec compresses the same pixels the encoder receives" checkable instead of merely asserted. The codec's own resampling is fixed by `params.preprocessing.codec_downsample_interpolation`, `codec_upsample_interpolation` and `codec_resize_preserves_aspect`, so the receiver-side upsample is not an implementer's choice inside a comparison BR-3 depends on. **This requirement is accepted at G-1 and named in W1's schedule row**: it existed but was scheduled nowhere, so W1 data could have flowed before the canonical-pixel contract was accepted. The classical codec MUST compress `params.preprocessing.codec_input` — the same canonical pixels the learned encoder receives — so BR-3's equal-channel-uses claim is not quietly comparing two different images. Reconstructions MUST be clipped per `params.preprocessing.reconstruction_clipped_before_metrics` before scoring, and PSNR and SSIM MUST use `params.preprocessing.psnr_data_range`, `params.preprocessing.ssim_impl` and `params.preprocessing.ssim_gaussian_weights`. Rationale: none of this was specified anywhere, and every item on the list changes a reported number — an unclipped reconstruction inflates PSNR, a mismatched `data_range` shifts it by decibels, and a codec fed differently-resized pixels from the encoder makes the whole comparison invalid rather than merely noisy (AM-28). *(verify: unit test asserting the canonical tensor is bit-identical on both paths for the same stable sample ID, plus a metrics test against a known-PSNR image pair)*
- **SR-20** — **Dataset provenance MUST be pinned, not assumed.** Each entry in `params.datasets` MUST name its `loader`, `loader_size_arg`, `source_url`, `archive_sha256`, `licence` and `published_val_becomes`, and the archive checksum MUST be verified at fetch and recorded in the run metadata. Rationale: the split counts and seed alone do not identify the data — a re-released archive, a different loader version or a changed class ordering all reproduce the counts while changing the images behind them, and every accuracy in this project is denominated in that data. Two corrections to previously held beliefs, both checkable in minutes and both wrong (AM-58): **`torchvision` does ship an Imagenette loader**, so `params.datasets.imagenette160.loader` uses it at `loader_size_arg` rather than a hand-rolled fetch, and the working note claiming otherwise was stale; and the checksums MUST be this project's own recorded values rather than an assumption that the loader verifies integrity, which its documentation does not state. `archive_sha256` is recorded as pending until the first W1 fetch and MUST be filled at G-1 — an unfilled checksum is a failing gate, not a default. *(verify: integrity test asserting each archive's recorded SHA-256 before use, a test that every dataset instantiates through the one registry path of SR-2, and a G-1 acceptance check that no `archive_sha256` is still pending)*
- **SR-21** — **The environment MUST be locked and reproducible from a clean checkout.** `params.environment` fixes `python_version`, the pinned versions of every runtime dependency, `torch_index_url`, and `lock_file` in `lock_format` with hashes. Installation MUST assert `params.environment.cuda_assertion` — a successful `import torch` is **not** the check, because a bare `pip install torch` resolves to the CPU build (AM-23) — and MUST record `params.environment.record_in_run_metadata` with every result. `params.environment.deterministic_backend` MUST be set, and reproduction is judged against `params.environment.reproduction_tolerance`: exact hashes for deterministic CPU fixtures, and validation top-1 within the stated tolerance for a same-seed GPU retrain, never below the G-1 floor. A CPU-only install path MUST exist for `params.environment.cpu_install_path_required_for`, materialised as `params.environment.cpu_lock_source` → `params.environment.cpu_lock_file` and committed (AM-67). **Three further constraints on the lockfile itself, all found by building it (AM-65, AM-66):** it MUST be resolved with `params.environment.lock_index_strategy`, because the resolver's default stops at the first index carrying a package *name* and the CUDA wheels differ only in their local version; it MUST embed its own index URLs (`params.environment.lock_emit_index_url`), or neither the resolver's own installer nor plain `pip` can satisfy it and the portability clause below is untestable; and it MUST cover the spec tooling as well as the runtime stack (`params.environment.lock_covers_spec_tooling`, `params.environment.pyyaml`), because a lockfile-exact install removes what it does not name. Rationale: `requirements.txt` carried the spec tooling alone while the W0 environment lived outside the repository, so nothing in the repository could rebuild the stack that produced its evidence — and SR-12 promised determinism against a lockfile that did not exist (AM-58). The lockfile is resolved by `params.environment.lock_tool` at or above `params.environment.lock_tool_version_min` from `params.environment.lock_source`, and the emitted `params.environment.lock_file` MUST remain installable by plain `pip install --require-hashes` — the resolver is pinned so that *resolution* reproduces, not so that the project acquires a runtime dependency on it (AM-61). *(verify: one documented command from a clean checkout that creates the environment, verifies hashes, materialises the SR-17 manifests, runs the data integrity and preprocessing tests, trains or resumes the W1 classifier and reproduces its validation metric within tolerance — all without reading a test sample; plus a check that the lockfile installs with `pip --require-hashes` alone)*
- **SR-22** — **Test access MUST be guarded by a committed freeze manifest.** No test sample may be loaded until `params.artifacts.freeze_manifest_file` exists and covers `params.evaluation.freeze_manifest_covers`; the guard MUST make the load *fail*, not warn. `params.evaluation.test_access_gate` names the gate that releases it. Rationale: DEC-12's rule is enforced by a structural guard rather than by discipline, because the failure it prevents is invisible after the fact — a curve seen early cannot be unseen, and no audit of the finished repository can distinguish a configuration chosen before test from one chosen after. If a genuine code defect is discovered after test opens, the affected campaign MUST be recorded as invalidated and **rerun complete**; selectively replacing favourable or unfavourable cells is prohibited under ER-8 (AM-58). *(verify: a test that loading a test sample without a valid freeze manifest raises; a CI check demonstrating that G-1 and the W10 rehearsal execute with zero test-loader reads; and an archived freeze manifest whose hashes resolve to the committed code, config, manifests and checkpoints)*
